title: Finite-sum monotone inclusions: component values and an exact resolvent.

description_paragraphs:

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
assumptions.description: The operator $F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n F_i$ is monotone, meaning $\langle F(u)-F(v),u-v\rangle\ge0$. Componentwise monotonicity is not assumed.

model.parameter_domain_description: $R$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $n$: positive integer. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table; additional accuracy and dimension conditions appear in each regime.
description_paragraphs: The condition $F=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nF_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ holds. The average $F$ is monotone; individual components need not be monotone.

$$
\frac1n\sum_i\|F_i(u)-F_i(v)\|_2^2\le\beta^2\|u-v\|_2^2\quad(\forall u,v\in\mathbb{R}^d).
$$
The public initial point is $0$. There exists $z^\star$ satisfying $0\in F(z^\star)+G(z^\star)$ and $\|z^\star\|_2\le R$.
The operator $G$ is maximally monotone and set-valued; its exact resolvent is a separate available interface.

description_paragraphs: Each $F_i(z)$ increments $N_{\rm component}$ by one; a full average costs $n$ calls. Calls to $J_{\eta G}$ are recorded separately as $N_{\rm resolvent}$. The primary scalar comparison projects onto component calls only.

Use expected work on the worst instance. The algorithm stops almost surely, with call count $\tau$ satisfying $\sup_I\mathbb{E}[\tau]\le N$. This does not require every execution path to finish within $N$ calls.
